services.label: GrabBike
services.notes: Grab's own fare guide (27 Aug 2026) says GrabBike is 25 THB for the first 2 km, and after that it uses 'the local tiered rate'. That tiered rate is the legal ceiling for motorcycle taxis (Ministerial Regulation 2016, still in force): 25 THB for 0-2 km, max 5 THB/km for 2-5 km, max 10 THB/km for 5-15 km, and max 10 THB/km past 15 km if no price is agreed. No per-minute charge or separate booking fee has been published. Real-world blog prices for Bangkok in 2026 (3 km 40-55, 5 km 50-70, 8 km 70-100 THB) run about 10-30% above this formula, which fits surge on top of the base schedule. The app quotes a fixed price up front.
sources: https://hilight.kapook.com/view/134566 (Kapook, 2 km 25 THB / 2-5 km 5 THB / 5-15 km 10 THB)

services.label: GrabBike Saver
services.notes: Grab advertises a starting price of 19 THB (campaign 1 Mar - 15 Apr 2026) and earlier a 'best price from 26 THB' (Jan-Mar 2025, Bangkok). You wait longer for a rider. The per-km tiers are MY ESTIMATE of about 10% below GrabBike, not published numbers.

services.label: GrabCar (JustGrab)
services.notes: Grab's guide (27 Aug 2026) gives 45 THB for 0-2 km, +8 THB/km for 2-6 km, +7 THB/km for 6-40 km and +10 THB/km above 40 km, and says a congestion charge is added separately. The DLT rule for app-hailed cars (Royal Gazette, Nov 2021, reaffirmed when registration became mandatory on 2 Oct 2025) sets: small car 40-45 THB for the first 2 km, 6-10 THB/km after that, 2 THB/min in traffic, 20 THB booking fee, and a surge cap of the lower of 200 THB or 1x the base fare. So the app minimum is effectively 60-65 THB with the booking fee. Check against 2026 blog prices: formula (45 + 3x8 + 20 + about 15 min x 2) = about 120 THB for 5 km, vs 120-160 THB reported.

services.label: GrabCar Saver
services.notes: Grab sells GrabCar Saver as 'cheaper for sure' but publishes no numbers. These figures are MY ESTIMATE of about 10-15% below JustGrab, kept inside the DLT band (40-45 base, 6-10 THB/km). You wait longer for a car.

services.label: GrabCar Premium / Plus
services.notes: Grab calls this a 'premium fixed price' and publishes no breakdown. Travel guides say Premium/SUV/Plus 'starts at 110 THB'. The per-km and per-min figures are MY ESTIMATE, set so the total comes out about 1.6-1.8x JustGrab. Low confidence.

surge.notes: Normal: 1.0x. Weekday rush (07-09, 17-20) and rain: about 1.2-1.5x (the blogs report +20-40% and +50-80%). Heavy rain, late night or holidays: up to 2x or more, as shown in the app. For cars, the DLT caps the peak add-on at the lower of 200 THB or 1x the base fare. Motorcycles have no published surge cap. For an estimator, show a range: fare x 1.0 up to fare x 1.4.

airport.notes: Not official. Taxifarefinder lists 100 THB (Economy) and 300 THB (Premium) for pickups at Suvarnabhumi, and there is no GrabBike at the official airport pickup point. Expressway tolls (usually 25-75 THB) are paid on top by the passenger. Short trips inside Lat Krabang normally use no tolls.

caveats: Grab shows a fixed price up front, calculated by its own algorithm. Published schedules only approximate it, so expect about +/-20% even without surge.
The GrabCar and GrabBike base schedules come from Grab's own fare guide (Aug 2026) and the government rules. The Saver and Premium per-km numbers are estimates (marked in notes).
The DLT car fare notice is from Nov 2021. No newer fare notice turned up, only the Oct 2025 rule making registration mandatory. The motorcycle fare ceiling dates from 2016.

Grab adds its own time/congestion charge. The DLT figure (2 THB/min in traffic) is used as a proxy, and only the time spent stuck in traffic should count, not the whole trip. For an estimator, charging perMin on about half of the trip time is reasonable.

The speed defaults are my assumptions for suburban Lat Krabang (Chalong Krung, Lat Krabang Rd, Romklao sois): about 20 km/h for a car and 25 km/h for a motorcycle, dropping to about 12-15 and 20 km/h at rush hour. Blog data for central Bangkok rush hour (5 km: car 25-45 min, bike 12-20 min) is slower.
The 1.35 detour factor is the usual urban road-to-straight-line ratio (1.3-1.4). Use 1.4-1.5 where the Airport Rail Link, the SRT tracks or the canals force long detours.
Bolt was left out. Its only published rate (30 THB base, 4 THB/km, 1.6 THB/min for economy car) comes from a 2020 BK Magazine article and is outdated. 2026 guides put Bolt about 10-20% below Grab.
